issues.legal_issue: A person whose lease has expired and who remains in possession without the landlord’s consent cannot rely on statutory protection against termination based merely on expiry when that person has no continuing tenancy.
material_facts: The agricultural lease was for five years and included an option to renew, which the tenant did not exercise; under the earlier statutory deeming provision, the lease term was extended to ten years and expired in 1953.
The tenant had been treated as a protected tenant, but that status ended when the trust-related exemption was introduced in 1956.
The tenant remained in possession after the contractual tenancy had ended, and the landlord had not consented to continued possession.
The landlord had given notices seeking termination and possession.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was in possession as a tenant by sufferance, not as a tenant holding over, and section 4B did not apply because no tenancy remained.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4B of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 prevents termination of a tenancy merely because its agreed or customary duration has expired; it does not apply where no tenancy exists. Under the common-law distinction applied by the Court, a person remaining in possession after termination without the landlord’s consent is a tenant by sufferance, whereas consent to continued possession is required for a tenant holding over or a tenant at will. The Court relied on the statutory history under section 23(1)(b) of the Bombay Tenancy Act, 1939, and sections 3A, 4A and 88B of the 1948 Act to determine the duration of the lease and the ending of protected status. It expressed no opinion on the application of section 84 of the Bombay Land Revenue Code or section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, and relied on no earlier case for this principle.

rule.if: tenancy_protection_claim and contractual_lease_expired and protected_status_ended and landlord_did_not_consent_to_continued_possession

predicates.tenancy_protection_claim: A person in possession claims legal protection against termination of a tenancy.
predicates.contractual_lease_expired: The agreed lease term, including any applicable statutory extension of that term, has ended.
predicates.protected_status_ended: A statutory status that had protected the occupant’s tenancy has ceased to apply.
predicates.landlord_did_not_consent_to_continued_po: The landlord did not agree to the occupant remaining in possession after the tenancy ended.
predicates.expiry_based_termination_protection_unav: The occupant cannot rely on protection against termination based merely on expiry because no tenancy remains.

issues.definition: When a tenancy-protection claim involves an expired lease, ended protected status, and no landlord consent to continued possession, expiry-based termination protection is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: An occupant who is a tenant by sufferance and does not dispute that the land belongs to a trust is not entitled to notice of the collector’s inquiry into whether the trust qualifies for an exemption certificate.
material_facts: The Collector held an inquiry to determine whether the trust met the conditions for a certificate under section 88B(2).
The tenant was in possession as a tenant by sufferance.
The tenant did not dispute that the lands were property of the trust.
issues.conclusion: The inquiry was between the Collector and the trust, and the tenant was not entitled to notice of it.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 88B(2) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, the Collector holds an inquiry to determine whether the trust satisfies the conditions in the proviso to section 88B(1), including registration as a public trust and appropriation of the lands’ entire income for the trust’s purposes. The Court held that this inquiry is between the Collector and the trust. The certificate’s conclusive-evidence effect means compliance with those conditions need not be proved again; no earlier case is relied on for this ruling.

predicates.trust_exemption_certificate_inquiry: An administrative inquiry is held to decide whether a trust qualifies for a certificate exempting its property from tenancy protections.
predicates.claimant_is_tenant_by_sufferance: The claimant remains in possession after the tenancy has ended without the landlord’s consent.
predicates.claimant_does_not_dispute_trust_ownershi: The claimant does not contest that the land belongs to the trust.
predicates.claimant_not_entitled_to_notice: The claimant has no entitlement to notice of the certificate inquiry.

issues.definition: When a tenant by sufferance does not dispute the trust’s ownership in an inquiry about an exemption certificate, the claimant is not entitled to notice of that inquiry.
